slides.title: TACTIC: Understanding Tactile Encoders and Conditioning for Contact-rich Robot Manipulation Policies
slides.tldr: STUDY ON TACTILE ENCODERS FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This research evaluates various tactile encoders and fusion strategies across real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks, finding that the optimal representation depends on the specific task.

card.one_liner: No single tactile encoder or fusion strategy is universally optimal; performance depends strongly on the task.
card.key_idea: A systematic real-world study evaluating five tactile encoders and five multimodal fusion strategies using Action Chunking Transformers (ACT) across four contact-rich manipulation tasks.
card.evaluation: 2,180 real-world rollouts across four tasks (board/vase wiping, USB-C insertion, screwing), comparing success rates and visual out-of-distribution robustness.
card.limitation: Contrastive-based fusion can induce task-specialist behavior, potentially causing failure in tasks with high spatial variation like board wiping.

slides.title: Tactile Sensing Array for Multi-Phalanx Sensing in Humanoid Hands
slides.highlight: This work presents a low-cost tactile array for humanoid fingers that provides feedback across multiple phalanges, supporting the embodied interaction goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, multi-phalanx tactile sensor for humanoid fingers using Velostat and 3D-printed structures.
card.key_idea: A piezoresistive array featuring a 2x3 matrix and tip sensor for the distal phalanx, with single contact lines for proximal and middle phalanges using a gap-and-bump structure.
card.evaluation: Tested via loading/unloading curves and contact patterns with cubes/cylinders. A 3D-printed gap-and-bump design reduced recovery time by 74% compared to flush-contact.
card.limitation: The sensor exhibits significant hysteresis and slow post-release relaxation, requiring future software-based compensation.

slides.title: Imp-ACT: Adaptive Impedance Control and Action Chunking with Transformers to Learn Contact-Rich Manipulation from Demonstrations
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a self-tuning impedance controller and transformer-based policy to learn direction-dependent stiffness, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition and compliant interaction.

card.one_liner: Imp-ACT learns contact-rich manipulation by jointly predicting motion and direction-dependent stiffness using Transformers.
card.key_idea: A self-tuning impedance controller generates adaptive stiffness during teleoperation; an ACT-based policy then learns to predict end-effector pose, gripper action, and motion-direction stiffness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on wiping and plug insertion against fixed low/high-stiffness baselines using success rates and contact forces; results show higher success and lower vibrations.

slides.title: Impedance Cloning: Learning Equilibrium Point Parameters for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: LEARNING BIOMECHANICAL PRIORS FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work proposes Impedance Cloning to imitate stiffness and equilibrium points, enabling robots to passively absorb contact uncertainty. It is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition and human-AI alignment in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: Impedance Cloning improves contact-rich manipulation by imitating latent stiffness and equilibrium point parameters instead of trajectories.
card.key_idea: A particle filter extracts latent stiffness and equilibrium point parameters from bilateral teleoperation data, redefining the imitation learning action space to enable passive compliance.
card.evaluation: Tested on CRANE-X7 manipulators across wiping, pick-and-place, and grasping tasks. Outperformed trajectory baselines in force stability and success rates (84/100 cups).
card.limitation: Contact may be lost if environmental deviations exceed the equilibrium point, reversing the restoring force away from the surface.

slides.title: VLaRL: Augmenting Vision-Language-Action Models with Simulation-Trained Latent-Conditioned Residual RL
slides.highlight: VLaRL improves the precision of frozen vision-language-action models in contact-rich tasks by training residual reinforcement learning in simulation and transferring it to real robots via latent representation alignment.

card.one_liner: VLaRL improves frozen VLA precision via simulation-trained residual RL using aligned vision-language latent representations.
card.key_idea: A lightweight mapper aligns simulation VLM latents to real distributions, enabling a residual RL policy trained in simulation to provide corrective actions during real-world deployment.
card.evaluation: Tested on four contact-rich tasks using Flower and GR00T N1.7 backbones. Real-world success improved across all combinations; ablations confirm latent alignment is critical.
card.limitation: Requires task-specific digital-twin reconstruction for paired sim-real trajectories and does not explicitly address discrepancies in physical contact dynamics.

slides.title: Praxis: Distilling Physical Interaction Priors from Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work utilizes egocentric video demonstrations and tactile feedback to achieve generalizable whole-body manipulation, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on ego-exo views and procedural skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: Praxis enables humanoid whole-body manipulation using one-shot egocentric video demonstrations without task-specific policy retraining.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical framework combining VLN-guided navigation, closed-loop posture calibration, and object-centric interaction priors distilled from RGB-D videos, enhanced by online visual and tactile feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested on five long-horizon tasks using a Unitree G1; achieved 76.97% mean success rate, outperforming YOTO (66.67%) and OKAMI (37.58%) across 33 trials per task.
card.limitation: Failures include collisions during approach, finger-handle disengagement, and accidental contact with adjacent object buttons.

slides.title: Res-HIL: Human-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning for Sample-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: HUMAN-GUIDED RESIDUAL RL FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: Res-HIL introduces a framework that learns corrective actions on top of a frozen imitation policy using human interventions for direct supervision and reward shaping. It demonstrates improved sample efficiency and performance in contact-rich manipulation tasks compared to full-policy RL.

card.one_liner: Res-HIL improves pretrained manipulation policies using human interventions as both direct supervision and reward signals.
card.key_idea: Learns a residual policy atop a frozen imitation policy, utilizing human corrections for behavior cloning and intervention-aware reward shaping to penalize preceding autonomous failures.
card.evaluation: Tested on five contact-rich tasks (e.g., peg-in-hole, cable routing) against HIL-SERL and ResFiT; outperformed baselines in success rates and training speed.

slides.title: Contact-Implicit Stein Projected ADMM for Discovery of Diverse Contact-Rich Manipulation Strategies
slides.highlight: This research introduces a solver combining Consensus ADMM with Stein variational inference to discover multiple distinct contact-rich solutions for tasks like pushing and grasping.

card.one_liner: Stein Projected ADMM discovers diverse, feasible contact-rich manipulation strategies by injecting repulsion into split variables.
card.key_idea: Combines Stein Variational Gradient Descent with ADMM, applying repulsive forces to the split variable $z$ before projecting onto the feasible set to ensure diversity without compromising feasibility.
card.evaluation: Tested on annulus/complementarity problems and tasks (pushing, grasping, pivoting, handover) against SteinSQP and ADMM. Results show better diversity and faster convergence.
